subject: evs
prompt_en: A friend in your class cannot hear. How could you tell them 'Let's play cricket after school'?
prompt_hi: Tumhari class mein ek dost sun nahi sakta. Use 'school ke baad cricket khelein?' kaise bataoge?
answer: Without sound: write it down, show it with gestures (batting action, point to the clock or outside), use the sign if you know it, or show a picture.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Long ago, before phones, how could people in one village quickly warn the next village about danger? Think of things that can be seen or heard from far away.
prompt_hi: Bahut pehle, jab phone nahi the, ek gaon wale paas ke gaon ko jaldi se khatre ki khabar kaise dete honge? Socho, aisi cheezein jo door se dikhein ya sunaai dein.
answer: By loud sounds or signs seen from far: beating drums, blowing a conch or horn, ringing bells, smoke signals, or sending a fast runner or rider.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Look at three road signs on the screen: a triangle with a walking person, a red circle with a horn crossed out, a triangle with two children carrying school bags. Tell me in words what each sign says.
prompt_hi: Screen pe 3 road sign dekho: triangle mein chalta hua aadmi, laal gol ghere mein kata hua horn, aur triangle mein bag liye do bachche. Har sign kya keh raha hai, shabdon mein batao.
answer: Walking person: people crossing ahead (pedestrian crossing). Horn crossed out: no honking. Children with bags: school ahead, drive slowly.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Sign language is just people waving their hands. Anyone can understand it, and it's the same in every country.' Find the mistakes.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Sign language toh bas haath hilaana hai. Koi bhi samajh sakta hai, aur har desh mein same hoti hai.' Galtiyan pakdo.
answer: Sign language is a real language with fixed signs and rules that have to be learnt; different countries have different sign languages, such as Indian Sign Language.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Two situations: telling your friend across a very noisy platform to come to you, and telling your aunt in Chennai that you passed your exam. Pick a good way for each. Why are they different?
prompt_hi: Do situation: shor wale platform ke us paar dost ko bulana, aur Chennai wali mausi ko batana ki tum pass ho gaye. Dono ke liye achha tareeka chuno. Dono alag kyon hain?
answer: Noisy platform: wave or point, because your friend can see you but not hear you. Chennai: phone call or message, because she is far away. The best way depends on the situation.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu how we can talk to someone without using any words. Give two examples.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin Golu ko samjhao ki bina shabdon ke kisi se baat kaise kar sakte hain. Do example do.
answer: Messages can be shared with gestures, facial expressions, signs and pictures, sign language or touch (Braille); e.g. waving goodbye, a red light meaning stop.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Remember our talk about ways of communicating? Name two ways that use words and two ways that don't.
prompt_hi: Yaad hai communication wali baat? Do tareeke batao jinme shabd hote hain, aur do jinme nahi.
answer: With words: talking, letters, phone calls, text messages. Without words: gestures, signs or pictures, sign language, facial expressions.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Where would you go to: post a rakhi to your cousin in another city? See a doctor for fever? Report a lost bicycle?
prompt_hi: Kahan jaoge: doosre shehar mein cousin ko rakhi bhejne? Bukhaar mein doctor ko dikhane? Khoyi hui cycle ki report karne?
answer: Post office; hospital, clinic or health centre; police station.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A farmer needs money to buy seeds, but his crop will only be ready months later. Predict: which neighbourhood place can help him, and how?
prompt_hi: Ek kisaan ko beej khareedne ke liye paise chahiye, par fasal toh mahino baad aayegi. Guess karo: mohalle ki kaunsi jagah uski madad karegi, aur kaise?
answer: A bank: it can give him a loan now, which he pays back later with a little extra called interest.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Predict what the colony park will look like after a month if everyone throws wrappers there and nobody cleans it.
prompt_hi: Guess karo, agar sab log park mein wrapper phenkein aur koi saaf na kare, toh ek mahine baad park kaisa dikhega?
answer: Dirty and smelly, with flies and mosquitoes; children cannot play there and it can become unsafe. Everyone has to help keep it clean.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why are places like parks, hospitals and post offices called 'public' places?
prompt_hi: Park, hospital aur post office jaisi jagahon ko 'public' jagah kyon kehte hain?
answer: Because they are for everyone to use and are not owned by one person; they are run for all the people (often by the government), so everyone must take care of them.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a chemist shop and a hospital. What can each do for you?
prompt_hi: Chemist ki dukaan aur hospital mein kya farak hai? Dono tumhare liye kya kar sakte hain?
answer: The chemist sells medicines (the ones a doctor has written); the hospital has doctors and nurses who check you, treat you and can keep you there if you are very sick.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your family has moved to a new town. Name three places you would want to find first, and say why.
prompt_hi: Tumhari family naye shehar mein shift hui hai. 3 jagah batao jo tum sabse pehle dhoondhoge, aur kyon.
answer: Any three with sensible reasons, e.g. hospital (health), school (studies), market or kirana (food), bank or ATM (money), police station (safety).

subject: evs
prompt_en: In a small village there is no big hospital nearby. Where might people go for health help, and what number can anyone in India call in an emergency?
prompt_hi: Ek chhote gaon mein paas mein bada hospital nahi hai. Wahan log ilaaj ke liye kahan jaate honge, aur India mein emergency mein kaunsa number milaate hain?
answer: A primary health centre (PHC) or the village health worker (ASHA didi); 112 is India's emergency number (many states also use 108 for an ambulance).

subject: evs
prompt_en: I'll describe a tiny map in words. Top row: school on the left, post office on the right. Bottom row: kirana on the left, park on the right. Draw it, then tell me which place is just above the park and which is just to the left of the park.
prompt_hi: Suno, ek chhota sa map shabdon mein. Upar wali line: left mein school, right mein post office. Neeche wali line: left mein kirana, right mein park. Ise banao, phir batao park ke theek upar kya hai aur park ke left mein kya hai?
answer: The post office is just above the park; the kirana is just to the left of the park.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'A bank just keeps your money locked in a big safe. That's all it does.' What did Golu miss?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Bank bas tumhare paise ek badi tijori mein band rakhta hai. Bas itna hi kaam hai.' Golu kya bhool gaya?
answer: A bank also lends money (loans) to people who need it, pays interest to savers and helps people send money; it does not just lock money away.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu what three public places in your neighbourhood do for people.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki tumhare mohalle ki 3 public jagahein logon ke liye kya karti hain.
answer: Three public places with a correct service each, e.g. the post office sends letters and parcels and keeps savings; the hospital treats sick people; the police station helps keep people safe.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From our last talk: what can you do at a post office, other than sending a letter?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baat se: post office mein chitthi bhejne ke alawa aur kya kar sakte hain?
answer: Send parcels, keep money in a savings account, send money (money order).

subject: evs
prompt_en: You want a cricket bat that costs ₹300. If you save ₹50 every week, how many weeks will it take?
prompt_hi: Tumhe ₹300 ka cricket bat chahiye. Agar har hafte ₹50 bachao, toh kitne hafte lagenge?
answer: 6 weeks.

subject: evs
prompt_en: You keep ₹1000 in a gullak and your brother keeps ₹1000 in a bank savings account for one year. Predict: after a year, who will have more, and why?
prompt_hi: Tum ₹1000 gullak mein rakhte ho aur tumhara bhai ₹1000 bank ke savings account mein, ek saal ke liye. Guess karo: saal ke baad kiske paas zyada honge, aur kyon?
answer: The brother: the bank adds a little interest, so he will have a bit more than ₹1000; the gullak still has exactly ₹1000.

subject: evs
prompt_en: You deposit five ₹100 notes in a bank. A month later you withdraw ₹500. Predict: will you get the same five notes back?
prompt_hi: Tumne bank mein ₹100 ke paanch note jama kiye. Ek mahine baad ₹500 nikaale. Guess karo: kya wahi paanch note wapas milenge?
answer: Almost certainly not the same notes, but the same amount: the bank keeps a record of how much is yours, not your exact notes.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why might a family prefer a bank account to keeping a lot of cash in a gullak at home?
prompt_hi: Ek family ghar pe gullak mein bahut saara cash rakhne ki jagah bank account kyon pasand karegi?
answer: The money is safer from theft, loss or damage, it is recorded in their name, and it earns a little interest.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Gullak versus savings account: tell me one good thing about each.
prompt_hi: Gullak aur savings account: dono ki ek-ek achhi baat batao.
answer: Gullak: easy, at home, good for small coins, you can see it fill up. Savings account: safe, earns interest, recorded in your name.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Meera saves ₹20 every week. Her birthday is in 8 weeks. Will she have enough for a ₹150 book?
prompt_hi: Meera har hafte ₹20 bachaati hai. Uska birthday 8 hafte baad hai. Kya ₹150 ki kitaab ke liye paise ho jayenge?
answer: Yes: 8 × ₹20 = ₹160, which is more than ₹150, with ₹10 left over.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A shopkeeper wants to make his shop bigger but doesn't have enough money. How can a bank help him, and how is that connected to people who save?
prompt_hi: Ek dukaandaar apni dukaan badi karna chahta hai par paise kam hain. Bank uski madad kaise karega, aur iska bachat karne walon se kya rishta hai?
answer: The bank gives him a loan from the money that savers have deposited; he pays it back over time with interest, and part of that interest is paid to savers.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Someone phones your mother and says, 'I'm calling from your bank. Tell me your ATM PIN and the OTP.' What should your family do?
prompt_hi: Koi mummy ko phone karke kehta hai: 'Main bank se bol raha hoon, apna ATM PIN aur OTP batao.' Family ko kya karna chahiye?
answer: Never share the PIN or OTP; real banks never ask for them. Hang up, and tell a trusted adult or contact the bank on its official number.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Here is Ravi's saving chart: Week 1 ₹10, Week 2 ₹20, Week 3 ₹10, Week 4 ₹30. Tell me in words what happened, and how much he saved in all.
prompt_hi: Ye Ravi ka saving chart hai: Hafta 1 ₹10, Hafta 2 ₹20, Hafta 3 ₹10, Hafta 4 ₹30. Shabdon mein batao kya hua, aur kul kitna bachaya?
answer: He saved a different amount each week, the most in week 4; the total is ₹70.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'I have nine ₹1 coins and you have only two ₹5 coins, so I'm richer because I have more coins!' Check Golu.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mere paas ₹1 ke nau sikke hain aur tumhare paas sirf ₹5 ke do. Mere paas zyada sikke hain, toh main ameer hoon!' Golu ko check karo.
answer: Golu has ₹9; two ₹5 coins make ₹10, so the two coins are more money. Count the value, not the number of coins.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Two children each get ₹50 a week. Asha spends ₹30 and saves ₹20. Bunty spends all ₹50. After 5 weeks, how much has each saved? Does saving mean not spending at all?
prompt_hi: Do bachchon ko har hafte ₹50 milte hain. Asha ₹30 kharch karke ₹20 bachaati hai. Bunty poore ₹50 kharch kar deta hai. 5 hafte baad kisne kitna bachaya? Kya saving ka matlab bilkul kharch na karna hai?
answer: Asha has saved ₹100 and Bunty ₹0. Asha still spent money, so saving means keeping some aside regularly, not never spending.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu what happens to money when we put it in a bank, and why it is safe even though the bank doesn't keep our exact notes.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki bank mein paise jama karne pe unka kya hota hai, aur bank humare wahi note nahi rakhta phir bhi paise safe kyon hain.
answer: The bank writes how much is ours in our account, uses the pooled money to give loans, pays us interest, and we can take out our amount whenever we need it.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Without looking back: name two places where we can save money, and one reason to save.
prompt_hi: Bina dekhe batao: paise bachaane ki do jagah, aur bachat ka ek kaaran.
answer: Places: a gullak (piggy bank), a bank savings account, a post office savings account. Reasons: the future, emergencies, buying something bigger.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A parrot has a strong, curved, hooked beak. What kind of food is it good for?
prompt_hi: Tote ki chonch mazboot, mudi hui aur hook jaisi hoti hai. Ye kis tarah ka khaana khaane ke liye achhi hai?
answer: Cracking nuts and hard seeds and biting into fruits.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Match each beak to its food. Kingfisher: long and pointed. Sparrow: short and cone-shaped. Eagle: sharp and hooked. Foods: seeds, fish, meat.
prompt_hi: Chonch ko khaane se milao. Kingfisher: lambi aur nukeeli. Gauraiya: chhoti aur cone jaisi. Cheel/baaz: tez aur mudi hui. Khaana: beej, machhli, maans.
answer: Kingfisher: fish. Sparrow: seeds. Eagle: meat (it tears flesh with its hooked beak).

subject: evs
prompt_en: Here's a bird you may not know. It has very long thin legs and a long pointed beak, and it stands still in shallow water. Predict: what does it eat, and how does it get its food?
prompt_hi: Ek aisi chidiya dekho jo shayad tumne na dekhi ho. Uski taangein lambi-patli hain, chonch lambi aur nukeeli, aur woh kam gehre paani mein chupchaap khadi rehti hai. Guess karo: woh kya khaati hai aur kaise pakadti hai?
answer: Fish, frogs or small water animals; it stands in the water and quickly stabs or grabs them with its long beak (like a heron or egret).

subject: evs
prompt_en: A cactus lives in a hot, dry desert. Before I show you, predict: will its leaves be big and thin like a banana leaf, or something else? Why?
prompt_hi: Cactus garam aur sookhe registaan mein rehta hai. Dikhane se pehle guess karo: kya uske patte kele ke patte jaise bade aur patle honge, ya kuch aur? Kyon?
answer: Not big thin leaves: its leaves are sharp spines and its stem is thick and fleshy, which stores water and loses very little water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put your hand in a bucket of water and push the water, first with your fingers spread wide apart, then with your fingers pressed together like a paddle. Predict first: which way will push more water?
prompt_hi: Paani ki baalti mein haath daalo aur paani ko dhakelo: pehle ungliyan door-door phaila ke, phir ungliyan chipka ke chappu jaisa banake. Pehle guess karo: kis tarah zyada paani dhakelega?
answer: Fingers pressed together like a paddle push more water; this is how a duck's webbed feet help it swim.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why does a woodpecker have a strong, chisel-like beak, and toes with two pointing forward and two backward?
prompt_hi: Kathfodwa (woodpecker) ki chonch chheni jaisi mazboot kyon hoti hai, aur uske do panje aage aur do peeche kyon hote hain?
answer: Its beak drills holes in tree bark to find insects; its toes grip the tree trunk so it can cling and climb.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a duck's feet and a hen's feet. What is different, and why?
prompt_hi: Batakh ke pair aur murgi ke pair mein kya farak hai, aur kyon?
answer: A duck has webbed feet for swimming; a hen has separate toes with claws for walking and scratching the ground for food.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A lotus grows in ponds. Its leaves are big, round and flat, with a waxy top where water drops roll off. How does this help the lotus?
prompt_hi: Kamal talaab mein ugta hai. Uske patte bade, gol aur chapte hote hain, aur upar se mome jaise, jahan se paani ki boondein lud jaati hain. Isse kamal ko kya fayda hai?
answer: The broad flat leaves rest on or above the water and catch lots of sunlight; the waxy coat keeps water from soaking or sitting on them.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Pine trees grow in cold, snowy mountains like those in Himachal. Their leaves are thin and needle-like. Why might needle leaves help in heavy snow?
prompt_hi: Cheed (pine) ke ped Himachal jaise thande, barfeele pahadon mein ugte hain. Unke patte patle, sui jaise hote hain. Bhaari barf mein sui jaise patte kaise madad karte honge?
answer: Snow slides off thin needles easily, so branches don't get loaded and break; needle leaves also lose less water in cold, dry winds.
